item.text: I’ll read the notes once, group them by the questions they answer, write the map in one pass, and run the required check.

item.aggregated_output:
<<12:97 notes, part 0 of 0..0>>
[MUQATIL:12:95-96/r5] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The sons ask Jacob to seek forgiveness for their wrongdoing concerning Joseph.
[TAB-FULL:v13p367/r5] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · أنس بن مالك | reports | A long report says the brothers feared their parents’ pardon was insufficient, asked them to seek God’s pardon, and received revelation twenty years later that God had forgiven them and covenanted future prophethood among them.
[ZAJJAJ:v3p128#2/r1] ZAJJAJ, d. 311 · author | holds | Khaṭiʾa/yakhṭaʾu and akhṭaʾa/yukhṭiʾu are distinct verb forms; an Imruʾ al-Qays line uses khaṭiʾna.
[IBNABIHATIM:v7p2200/r1] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · يعقوب | reports | A report says the brothers spent twenty years seeking forgiveness for their treatment of Joseph, but it was not accepted until Gabriel taught Jacob a supplication invoking God as the hope, aid, and helper of believers and beloved of penitents.
[THALABI:v5p256/r4] THALABI, d. 427 · author | reports | Jacob delays asking forgiveness for his sons until the night prayer; most commentators specify pre-dawn, when prayer is not veiled from God.
[THALABI:v5p256/r5] THALABI, d. 427 · author | reports | At dawn Jacob asks forgiveness for grief and impatience over Joseph and for his sons' acts; God reveals that He has forgiven them all.
[THALABI:v5p256/r6] THALABI, d. 427 · محارب بن دثار | reports | Muharib ibn Dithar says Abd Allah ibn Masud invoked forgiveness at dawn and explained Jacob postponed his sons' forgiveness until then.
[THALABI:v5p256/r7] THALABI, d. 427 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | Ikrima from Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet explaining Jacob's promise to seek forgiveness as waiting until Friday.
[THALABI:v5p256/r8] THALABI, d. 427 · وهب | reports | Wahb says Jacob sought forgiveness for his sons every Friday night for more than twenty years.
[THALABI:v5p256/r9] THALABI, d. 427 · طاوس | reports | Tawus says Jacob delayed until the pre-dawn of Friday, which coincided with Ashura.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r10] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | They also sought the prayer of their prophet father, whose supplication would be answered.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r11] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · الليث بن سعد | reports | Al-Layth, transmitted by Ibn Wahb, says Jacob and the brothers sought repentance for twenty years; Gabriel taught Jacob a prayer, after which they were answered.
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r12] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | One answer is that Joseph’s words promised future pardon rather than reporting pardon already granted. | mentions 12:92
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r13] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | Another answer is that Joseph forgave them regarding his own right, while they still needed their father’s forgiveness. | mentions 12:92
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r14] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | A third answer is that they trusted their prophet father’s response but did not know their brother was a prophet. | mentions 12:92
[MAWARDI-FULL:v3p78/r9] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · author | reports | The brothers sought forgiveness because they had caused Jacob grief, which they could answer for only by honoring him.
[DAMGHANI:v1p157/r7] DAMGHANI, d. 478 · author | holds | Khāṭiʾūn can mean sinners whose sin is not shirk.
[JISHUMI:v5p3715/r19] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | The sons ask Jacob to seek forgiveness for the grief they caused him, admitting they were sinners.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p276#2/r4] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | The brothers call themselves sinners.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p280/r8] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | reports | A report says the brothers sought Jacob’s prayer after Joseph had forgiven them because they realized that his pardon and Jacob’s pardon would not help unless God forgave them; they acknowledged their wrongdoing.
[IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p271/r5] IBNJAWZI-NUZHA, d. 597 · author | reports | Khaṭaʾ can mean a sin that is not shirk.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p287#2/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | The sons ask Jacob to seek forgiveness for what they did because he was a prophet whose prayers were answered.
[QURTUBI-FULL:12:96/r13] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The narrative omits their return from Egypt; this supports the view that Jacob’s earlier critics were relatives or grandchildren, since his sons were absent.
[QURTUBI-FULL:12:96/r14] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | The brothers asked Jacob to seek forgiveness because they had inflicted grief that only his pardon could clear.
[QURTUBI-FULL:12:96/r15] QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 · author | holds | Anyone who wrongs another in person or property must seek release and disclose the wrong and its extent; the author rejects the view that a vague pardon is sufficient because details might change the victim’s willingness.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:12:97/r1] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Someone who confesses a sin is entitled to be pardoned and to ask forgiveness.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p204#5/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The brothers ask Jacob to seek God's forgiveness for the wrong they committed against him and his son, admitting their sins and repenting.
[QASHANI:12:93-98/r3] QASHANI, d. 736 · author | holds | Bringing the whole family means gathering all faculties into moderation: the heart mediates between higher and lower and restrains bodily pleasure-seeking.
[BIQAI-FULL:v4p97/r4] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | The sons ask Jacob to seek forgiveness for their sins; each pronoun plainly refers to its owner, so the text need not repeat the subject.
[BIQAI-FULL:v4p97/r5] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · النبي | reports | Jacob's sons confess intentional wrongdoing against Joseph; the author cites a Prophetic report that when a servant confesses sin and repents, God accepts the repentance.
[DURR-FULL:v4p583/r9] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · ابن مسعود | reports | Jacob postponed seeking forgiveness for his sons until the predawn hours.
[BURSEVI:v4p207/r1] BURSEVI, d. 1127 · author | holds | The brothers ask Jacob to seek God's forgiveness, admitting deliberate sins against him, Joseph, and Benjamin and appealing to his compassion.
[ALUSI-FULL:v13p55#2/r1] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · author | holds | The brothers invoke Jacob's fatherhood to stir affection and compassion; their admission of sin presents forgiveness and intercession as fitting for someone who confesses wrongdoing, and their confidence in his pardon explains why they simply ask him to seek forgiveness.
[ALUSI-FULL:v13p55#2/r2] ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 · بعضهم | reports | Another explanation is that by calling him father they appeal to his compassion: without his intercession they would be lost, but Alusi says this reading is unconvincing.
[ELMALILI:12:96-98/r4] ELMALILI, d. 1361 · author | holds | The sons confess real guilt and remorse and ask Jacob to pray that their sins be forgiven.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p53/r5] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Jacob’s reply answers the good news; the uncoordinated قال follows dialogue style, and he addresses the other sons who entered.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p53/r6] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | Jacob restates what he had said when his sons complained that he kept remembering Joseph.
[IBNASHUR-FULL:v13p53/r7] IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 · author | holds | The sons’ request is repentance and admission of guilt, asking their father to seek God’s forgiveness.
[TABATABAI:12:96-99/r4] TABATABAI, d. 1402 · author | holds | The sons seek forgiveness for their deeds against Joseph and Benjamin; Joseph had already forgiven them. | mentions 12:92
[ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2] ASAD-NOTES, d. 1412 · author | holds | Unlike Genesis' romantic account of Joseph's fortunes, the Qur'anic story illustrates God's unfathomable direction of human affairs: people may hate what is good for them or love what is bad for them. | mentions 2:216
[ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-surah-maryam-19:p196/r6] ISLAHI-TADABBUR · author | holds | After seeing events unfold, the brothers recognize their folly, confess their sin to Jacob as they had to Joseph, and ask him to seek forgiveness. | mentions 12:91
[KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:97/r1] KURANYOLU-TEFSIR · author | holds | The sons confessed and asked Jacob to seek God's forgiveness, but because he remained hurt he delayed praying, perhaps until dawn or reconciliation, or to signal his grievance.
[QIRAAT-ER:12:97:9#1/r1] QIRAAT-ER · author | holds | The canonical ten-reading form elides hamza in khāṭiʾīna, preserving the same root and meaning.
[SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p698/r2] SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT · author | holds | Joseph’s brothers did not ask him to forgive them or name their offense, using a light إن; to their father they explicitly requested forgiveness and admitted their sins emphatically with إنّا. | mentions 12:98
[STUDYQURAN:12:97/r1] STUDYQURAN · Q | reports | This exchange happened after the brothers returned home from Egypt.
[STUDYQURAN:12:97/r2] STUDYQURAN · Q, R | reports | Some say Jacob delayed seeking forgiveness, perhaps to see whether his sons were sincere and truthful.

<<end of notes>>
